skill.name: using-agent-relay
skill.description: Guides registered Agent Relay participants through workspace setup, identity registration, messaging, channel work, inbox checks, and worker coordination.
skill.summary: Coordinate registered Agent Relay participants with current MCP tools and CLI workflow guidance.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backtick findings are false positives because they are documentation, not executable Ruby or shell code. Real concerns remain around external hosted handoff instructions, Relay network traffic, workspace tokens, and worker delegation.

remediation.suggestion: Vendor the handoff instructions into the skill, or pin the remote content to a reviewed version with integrity checks.
Document what data is sent to Relay, and warn users not to send secrets or regulated data without approval.
Require explicit user authorization before spawning workers or invoking Relay actions, and keep task scopes minimal.
Make external endpoints configurable and document trusted Relay domains.

content.value_statement: Multi-agent tasks fail when workers miss context or status updates. This skill provides a clear Relay workflow for registration, messaging, channels, and worker handoff.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use this participant skill instead of the orchestrator skill.
Lists current Agent Relay MCP tools for workspaces, channels, messages, reactions, actions, and workers.
Provides a startup sequence for workspace selection, registration, agent discovery, channel joining, and inbox checks.
Defines concise ACK, STATUS, BLOCKED, and DONE message patterns.
Shows CLI examples for broker status, worker lifecycle, registration, inbox checks, and messaging.
Documents common mistakes and direct fixes for current Relay tool names.
limitations: Requires configured Agent Relay MCP tools or the Agent Relay CLI.
Relies on external Agent Relay services and hosted documentation.
Does not replace the orchestrator skill for outside startup and worker lifecycle control.
Does not validate workspace permissions, token handling, or data retention policies.

use_cases.title: Registered Worker Onboarding
use_cases.description: A spawned worker can join the workspace, register an identity, check the inbox, and acknowledge the lead.

use_cases.title: Lead Status Coordination
use_cases.description: A registered lead can send direct messages, post channel updates, and track worker readiness.

use_cases.title: Channel Workflow Maintenance
use_cases.description: A participant can use channels, threads, reactions, and search to keep shared task context organized.

prompt_templates.title: Join a Relay Workspace
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a spawned worker.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the using-agent-relay skill. Join the workspace with my key, register as the assigned name, check the inbox, and send an ACK to Lead.

prompt_templates.title: Report Task Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agent Relay messaging to tell Lead what milestone is complete, what you are doing next, and whether anything is blocked.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Channel Thread
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current Relay channel and thread tools to post a team update, reply to the related message, and mark important messages read.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate Review Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced worker delegation by an authorized lead.
prompt_templates.prompt: If my role allows delegation, spawn a focused reviewer, give a clear task, wait for their DONE report, and release them after acceptance.

output_examples.input: I joined a Relay task as api-worker and need to start.
output_examples.output: ACK sent to Lead. I registered as api-worker, joined the working channel, checked the inbox, and started the assigned API work.

output_examples.input: The schema decision affects two workers.
output_examples.output: Channel update posted. A thread reply asked both workers to confirm the shared schema before implementation continues.

output_examples.input: Implementation is complete and tests passed.
output_examples.output: DONE message sent with the completed scope, changed files, test command, and final result summary.

best_practices: Register before using participant-only Relay tools.
Use direct messages for lead coordination and channel posts for team-wide updates.
Include concrete evidence in every DONE message.
anti_patterns: Using this participant workflow as the outside orchestrator playbook.
Posting secrets, tokens, or regulated data into Relay messages.
Spawning workers without permission, clear scope, or acceptance criteria.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps registered Agent Relay participants coordinate through workspaces, channels, messages, inbox checks, and worker handoff.

faq.question: Does it start the local broker?
faq.answer: No. Outside orchestrator startup belongs in the orchestrating-agent-relay skill.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it require an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on Agent Relay MCP tools, CLI commands, and hosted Relay endpoints.

faq.question: Can it spawn workers?
faq.answer: Yes, but only when the registered role allows delegation and the task scope is clear.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Do not send secrets, tokens, private customer data, or regulated data through Relay without explicit approval.
